name: Synaptex-OC
description: Synaptex-OC is a CNT-organic hybrid substrate developed by BioForge Labs in partnership with Apex Nanofabrication, produced by functionalizing multi-walled CNT scaffolds with engineered extracellular matrix proteins that actively recruit and bond with living tissue at the molecular level. Implanted panels or filaments of Synaptex-OC integrate directly with surrounding bone, nerve, and muscle over a 2-4 week osseointegration period, creating a seamless organic-synthetic junction that eliminates the chronic micro-rejection and signal degradation seen with earlier augment interfaces. It is the premier substrate for neural bridge electrodes, bone-anchored prosthetics, and structural cyberware that must mechanically load through living skeletal tissue.
applications: cochlear and ocular augment mounting substrates
cost: Φ2,400 per gram (medical-grade sheet); Φ8,000 per unit (pre-formed implant blanks)
story_hooks: A batch of Synaptex-OC implants has been contaminated somewhere in the supply chain — instead of integrating cleanly, they are triggering aggressive inflammatory responses six weeks post-implant. Dozens of patients across the city are in crisis, and BioForge Labs is burying the recall to protect a product launch.

Black-market Synaptex-OC is being sold in the Shelf at one-tenth the price — but it's been synthesized without the anti-rejection protein coating. People are having it implanted by unlicensed surgeons, and the tissue bonding is going catastrophically wrong in ways that are difficult to reverse.

A runner discovers their own Synaptex-OC neural bridge contains an undocumented secondary conductive layer — someone has been passively recording their neural traffic for months. The data has already left the city.
